title: Artificial Intelligence Methods and Applications, B.S. (College of Information Sciences and Technology)
notes: University Park. The entire A-I and AIMA departments were missing from the catalog -- added minimal entries in new a-i_catalog.json/aima_catalog.json sourced from PSU course description pages. Real data gap: 'STAT 401' requires MATH 111 or MATH 141 (Calc II), but the bulletin's own suggested plan never schedules either anywhere -- added MATH 141 as an explicit Semester 3 item, same class of fix as Food Science's BMB 400 and CED's AEE 360 additions earlier this session. Chose the Capstone track (AIMA 430/440) over the Research Project track (A-I 494 x2) for the Fourth Year requirement. New engine-adjacent bug class found: 'AIMA 430' (needs A-I 375 completed in a PRIOR term, not same-term) was originally scheduled directly after A-I 375 with enough leftover Semester 6 credit headroom that the engine's greedy scan pulled AIMA 430 into the SAME simulated term as A-I 375 -- since prereqs (unlike concurrent requirements) only check credit already banked from earlier terms, this silently fell back to the A-I 494 alternate and permanently starved the real AIMA 430/440 capstone sequence, an infinite loop identical in shape to Energy Business and Finance's METEO 469 bug. Fixed at the DATA level (not the engine) by padding Semester 6 to 18 credits (over the 17cr/term cap) so the scan closes that term before ever reaching AIMA 430, guaranteeing A-I 375 lands in 'completed' one full term before AIMA 430 is considered. 9 credits of 'Support Course -- Technical' and 9 credits of 'Support Course -- Application' (from a student-chosen focus area: Agriculture, National Security, Business, Healthcare, Philosophy, Psychology, etc.) are modeled generically, same convention as CMPSC's own open pools. Post-parens-fix re-scrape (AND/OR prereq-parsing bug fix) uncovered the REAL shape of the AIMA 430 loop, superseding the padding-only diagnosis above: AIMA 430's actual catalog prereq is just CMPSC 445/448/DS 310 (no A-I 375 requirement at all -- that was only ever mentioned in the course description prose, not a formal prereq_groups entry), and NONE of those three were ever completable anywhere in this plan (all three need MATH 220 plus a STAT 318/414/418-class course, none present) -- so AIMA 430 was NEVER actually eligible, and the 'A-I 494' fallback kept winning by default in early terms, before plan_progress's own per-course dedup (a completed course can satisfy only one item) permanently starved Semester 8's AIMA 440/A-I 494 item once Semester 7's item claimed A-I 494 first -- a duplicate-fallback loop shape identical to Accounting's ACCTG 406 case. Real fix: added MATH 220 (Semester 3) and STAT 318 (Semester 4) to make CMPSC 445 genuinely completable (both satisfiable from courses already in this plan), then removed the 'A-I 494' fallback from both Semester 7/8 items entirely (options now just ['AIMA 430'] / ['AIMA 440']) so the engine can no longer silently substitute it -- matches the test suite's own explicit intent (test_aima_capstone_does_not_loop asserts AIMA 430 itself must appear, not A-I 494). Also found STAT 200/DS 200 (Semester 2, needed for A-I 370) need MATH 21, itself needing MATH 4, itself needing MATH 3 -- added the real chain explicitly: MATH 3 (Semester 1), MATH 4 (Semester 2), MATH 21 (Semester 3), same convention as every other hidden-prereq-chain addition this session (e.g. ABSM, ACCTG, ACTSC, ADPR, AE, AERSP, AGBM, AIE, LSCPE). Adds 15cr beyond the bulletin's own stated total, documented rather than silently absorbed. Bumped max_credits_per_semester to 18 to keep the resulting load realistic given the additions. STALENESS FIX (post 8caf0ae5, 'Add real PSU ALEKS math placement waivers; fix MATH 3/4 requirement bug'): MATH 3 and MATH 4 were added here as plan items to build a prereq chain into MATH 21 -- but that commit made planner_engine.expand_math_placement() unconditionally waive MATH 3 and MATH 4 for every student (their own catalog descriptions say they 'may not be used to satisfy the basic minimum requirements for graduation in any baccalaureate degree program'), and confirmed via the current catalog that MATH 21 itself has an EMPTY prereq_groups (its real prereq, 'MATH 4 or satisfactory performance on the mathematics placement examination', is a placement gate, not a literal course requirement -- same fact already verified for DATSC). So MATH 3 and MATH 4 were dead, unschedulable-for-a-real-reason plan items inflating this major's total credit count by 6 credits for no functional purpose -- removed both, kept MATH 21 (which is genuinely still required, per ACCTG 211/STAT 200's real prereq_groups). HANDBOOK VERIFICATION PASS: checked both the live bulletin and ist.psu.edu's own 'aima-major-requirements' advising page for an enumerated Technical/Application Support Course list (the CMPSC-equivalent handbook granularity) -- neither publishes one. The bulletin only names the broad fields involved (Technical: Computer Science, Data Sciences, Electrical Engineering, Math; Application: Agricultural Sciences, Business Fundamentals, Enterprise Technology Integration, National Security, Philosophy, Psychology), with 'Application' explicitly required to come from a single subject area chosen with an adviser -- none of those application-focus departments (AGSC/AGBM, BA/ACCTG, ETI, PHIL, PSYCH) are even in this plan's own departments list. Unlike CYBER/ETI/IEC/HCDD/SRA/DATSC's Application Focus slots (each backed by a real, bulletin- or department-published course-by-course list this pass), AIMA's genuinely has no such list to source from -- converting these to CMPSC's open_elective mechanism would either recommend an inappropriate course from an unrelated already-loaded department (ENGL/CAS/ESL) or require inventing a department allowlist/course list not found in any real source. Left as generic unfilled placeholders rather than guessing -- the correct call per this pass's 'never fabricate' instruction. Also re-verified: the required-course sequence (CMPSC 131/132/360/445/448/462/465, MATH 140/141/225/220/21, STAT 401/318, DS 200/305/310, A-I 100/341W/370/375, AIMA 430/440) still matches the current live bulletin's Suggested Academic Plan exactly; no staleness found there.
